However, three architectural smells weigh heavy: (1) OrderService at 2837 LOC + FrontendOrderService at 1391 LOC = 4228 LOC of near-duplicate order lifecycle code = sync drift vector; (2) Repository layer ABSENT — service-locator and direct Eloquent in 26 controllers means BranchScope coverage relies entirely on global-scope discipline and the Sentinel test (CLAUDE.md §9 — 20 models pinned); a missing-scope regression in any controller-direct-query is invisible to service-layer tests; (3) 16 `app(*::class)` calls inside controllers + 58 inside services indicate DI bypass that hides true coupling graph from static analysis.

findings.title: OrderService 2837 LOC + FrontendOrderService 1391 LOC = duplicate-lifecycle sync vector
findings.evidence: Both services own order creation, cancellation, status transition, loyalty refund, and cash-back hooks. RefundWithCounterEntryService:332-335 explicitly notes BOTH OrderService:1702/1805 AND FrontendOrderService:707 call refundPoints AFTER cashBack — duplicated discipline across two 800-2800-LOC files. Any sync-critical change (status enum extension, payment_method bucket, fiscal_sequence allocation) must be applied twice with no compile-time guard. The KdsOrderRecalled HEAL-5 succeeded because it was dispatched from KitchenDisplaySystemOrderService (single owner), but the same pattern applied to refund/cancel would carry a 50% drift risk.
findings.remediation: V1.0.2 backlog — extract OrderLifecycleService shared between POS and Kiosk paths (Architect agent specialty). Pin with `tests/Feature/Order/OrderServiceVsFrontendOrderServiceParitySentinelTest.php` to fail-CI when one mutates without the other.

findings.title: Repository layer 0/152 ratio — BranchScope discipline is the ONLY guard against multi-tenant leak
findings.evidence: Task spec assumed 152/2 ratio; actual filesystem shows app/Repositories does not exist (find returns empty). 26 controllers query Eloquent models directly (Order/Item/User/Payment/Branch/Customer/StockLevel/Coupon/Category/Setting — 59 raw queries total). Frontend/ItemController, Frontend/LoyaltyController (15 hits), Frontend/UpsellController, Frontend/MenuController are the worst offenders. Multi-tenant safety rests entirely on BranchScope global + BranchScopeCoverageSentinelTest pinning 20 models. A controller using `User::where(...)->lockForUpdate()->first()` (LoyaltyController:277) inside a non-scoped path would silently cross-branch if scope ever regressed.
findings.remediation: Either (a) ratchet a Repository layer for the 10 highest-traffic models (Order, Item, User, Payment, StockLevel, Coupon, Category, Branch, OrderItem, OrderPayment) or (b) add a static-analysis sentinel banning `Model::where|::find|::query` inside Http/Controllers (allow only in Services). Option (b) is V1.0.2 chip-away — preserves V1 ship date.

findings.title: Service-locator usage hides true coupling — 58 `app(*::class)` in Services + 16 in Controllers
findings.evidence: Including the documented-and-necessary `app(SealedOrderGuard::class)` at RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:73, 58 service-locator calls exist inside Services. Each call is INVISIBLE to constructor-injection cycle detection — meaning the cycle scan above is a LOWER BOUND. Hidden runtime cycles (A injects B at construct, B resolves A via app() at call time) cannot be ruled out without per-call tracing. The session-new RefundWithCounterEntryService → SealedOrderGuard service-locator is documented and justified, but it sets a precedent that propagates.
findings.remediation: Add a CI script grep counting `app(*::class)` inside app/Services — baseline at current count, fail on growth. Force new injections to flow through constructors. Documented exceptions (factory/circular) require a `// @service-locator-allowed: <reason>` comment to pass.

findings.title: Stock low-alert listener correctly suppressed for V1 binary stock — but no observability hook for the suppression itself
findings.evidence: app/Listeners/NotifyStockLowOnStockLevelChanged.php:57 short-circuits when threshold_low <= 0 (V1 Le Cayenne binary stock — all rows have threshold_low=0). Listener is activated by HEAL-2 (FK_CATALOG_STOCK_LOW_ALERT_ENABLED=true) for V1.0.2 admin-UI threshold ramp-up. Currently fires zero log lines in production. A future regression that accidentally sets threshold_low > 0 on a row would generate alerts with no test pinning the V1 zero-emission baseline.
findings.remediation: tests/Feature/Stock/StockLowAlertV1ZeroEmissionSentinelTest — assert that across all StockLevel rows in V1 seed, NotifyStockLowOnStockLevelChanged emits zero Log::warning. Already partially covered by StockRuptureAlertListenerSentinelTest (no double-broadcast) but not by an emission-count sentinel.
